findings.title: Invalid ERB syntax `<%- end if %>` raises a SyntaxError when rendering `embed/best`
findings.body: In `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` on line 6, the `if` block opened on line 2 is closed with `<%- end if %>`. `end if` is not valid Ruby syntax (`if` is not an expression here, and Ruby closes conditionals with `end` alone). Rendering `embed/best` when a topic exists will fail at template compilation time with a `SyntaxError`.

findings.title: Unescaped `request.referer` interpolated into JavaScript string enables reflected XSS
findings.body: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` line 11, `<%= request.referer %>` is interpolated directly inside a single-quoted JavaScript string literal: `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. Standard ERB HTML escaping does not escape backslashes, newlines, or `</script>`, and in Rails 3 (still supported per the `Gemfile`) single quotes are not escaped by `ERB::Util.html_escape` either. Because `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` only validates `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, an attacker can craft a URL on the embeddable host whose path or query string contains characters such as `</script><script>...` (or `'` / `\`) and cause arbitrary JavaScript to execute in the context of the Discourse origin when the iframe loads. Use `to_json` / ` escape_javascript` (or pass the origin derived from `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) instead of interpolating `request.referer` directly.

findings.title: `raw_html` cook method bypasses HTML sanitization, allowing stored XSS from RSS feeds or edited posts
findings.body: In `app/models/post.rb` line 133, `Post#cook` returns `raw` untouched when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, skipping `PrettyText.cook` and its HTML sanitizer as well as `:after_post_cook` plugin filters. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` lines 35-36) feeds `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` from an external RSS/Atom feed directly into `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Any `<script>`, `onload=`, `onerror=`, or `javascript:` URL present in the feed (or introduced later by any user who can edit that first post in Discourse) is stored verbatim in `cooked` and rendered unescaped into the forum and into `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` (`<%= raw post.cooked %>`), resulting in stored XSS.

findings.title: `PollFeed` crashes with `NoMethodError` on RSS 2.0 feeds or entries without `<content>`
findings.body: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` line 35, `i.content.scrub` assumes every parsed item has a non-nil `content` string. `SimpleRSS` only populates `i.content` / `content_encoded` when Atom `<content>` or `<content:encoded>` is present; standard RSS 2.0 items use `i.description` (or `i.summary`), leaving `i.content` as `nil`. In addition, `String#scrub` is a Ruby 2.1 method and raises `NoMethodError` on Ruby 1.9/2.0. When `i.content` is `nil`, polling the feed raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil:NilClass` and aborts the entire job before importing remaining items.
